# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# U7 — the N>2 extension the 2-agent case structurally could not show.
#
# The 2-agent, single-conflict scenario above has NO unrelated component, so declared bounds
# never change anything (the honest negative measure_footprints reports). At N>2 with multiple
# INDEPENDENT conflicts plus a disjoint unrelated region, declared bounds do change an
# observable: the unrelated component finalizes as soon as ITS OWN author is done, instead of
# waiting on the still-live conflicting agents (which, unbounded, are ⊤ and keep every component
# open until quiescence). Bounds never change WHICH effects land or the merged text (soundness,
# streaming.py docstring) — only the EPOCH at which an unrelated component closes. This is the
# eager-admit headroom U8's scheduler would exploit, measured here before U8 is built.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
@dataclass
class ComponentCloseMeasurement:
    label: str
    n_agents: int
    unrelated_agents: tuple
    close_step_unbounded: int   # schedule step at which the LAST unrelated effect committed
    close_step_bounded: int
    eager_admits_unbounded: int
    eager_admits_bounded: int
    merged_identical: bool      # soundness: bounds must not change the committed text
    closed_earlier: bool        # did declaring bounds close the unrelated component sooner?


def build_planted_scenario(*, n_conflict_regions: int, n_unrelated: int):
    """A single file with `n_unrelated` disjoint regions (one solo author each) and
    `n_conflict_regions` regions each co-written by two agents who write the SAME body cell
    to DIFFERENT values (an independent planted conflict). Returns
    `(base, agent_afters, unrelated_agents, schedule)`, where `schedule` emits + finishes every
    UNRELATED agent first, then the conflicting agents — so the moment the unrelated components
    are eligible to close (their authors done) the conflicting agents are still live. That gap
    is exactly what declared bounds turn into an earlier close."""
    funcs, agent_afters, unrelated_agents, order = [], {}, [], []

    def _file(bodies: dict[str, str]) -> str:
        return "\n\n".join(f"def {name}(x):\n    return {body}" for name, body in bodies.items()) + "\n"

    bodies = {}
    for i in range(n_unrelated):
        bodies[f"u{i}"] = "x + 1"
    for j in range(n_conflict_regions):
        bodies[f"c{j}"] = "x + 1"
    base = _file(bodies)

    for i in range(n_unrelated):
        agent = f"W{i}"
        b = dict(bodies); b[f"u{i}"] = f"x + {100 + i}"
        agent_afters[agent] = _file(b)
        unrelated_agents.append(agent)
        order.append(agent)
    for j in range(n_conflict_regions):
        for k, delta in ((0, 10), (1, 20)):  # two agents, DIFFERENT values → conflict on c{j}
            agent = f"P{j}_{k}"
            b = dict(bodies); b[f"c{j}"] = f"x + {delta + j}"
            agent_afters[agent] = _file(b)
            order.append(agent)

    # schedule: every unrelated agent emits + done FIRST, then every conflict agent emits, then
    # all conflict agents done, then quiesce.
    schedule = []
    for a in unrelated_agents:
        schedule.append(("effect", a))
        schedule.append(("done", a))
    conflict_agents = [a for a in order if a not in unrelated_agents]
    for a in conflict_agents:
        schedule.append(("effect", a))
    for a in conflict_agents:
        schedule.append(("done", a))
    return base, agent_afters, tuple(unrelated_agents), schedule


def _run_schedule(base, agent_afters, schedule, unrelated_agents, use_bounds):
    from eico.streaming import Coordinator
    base_art = project(base)
    lifts = {a: lift_file(base, after, agent=a) for a, after in agent_afters.items()}
    effects_by_agent = {a: r.eico_effects() for a, r in lifts.items()}
    bounds = None
    if use_bounds:
        bounds = {a: _actual_bound(base_art, r) for a, r in lifts.items()}
    coord = Coordinator(base_art, agent_bounds=bounds, agents=set(agent_afters))

    unrelated = set(unrelated_agents)
    close_step = None
    step = 0
    for kind, a in schedule:
        step += 1
        if kind == "effect":
            for e in effects_by_agent[a]:
                coord.on_effect(e)
        else:
            coord.on_agent_done(a)
        committed = {e.agent for e in coord.log.applied}
        if close_step is None and unrelated <= committed:
            close_step = step
    coord.quiesce()
    if close_step is None:
        step += 1
        close_step = step  # the unrelated component only closed at quiescence
    return close_step, coord.log.eager_admits, coord


def measure_component_close(*, n_conflict_regions: int = 2, n_unrelated: int = 1,
                            label: str = "") -> ComponentCloseMeasurement:
    """Drive the planted N>2 scenario under `bound=None` vs declared bounds and report whether
    the unrelated component closed earlier with bounds (the N>2 effect). Merged text must be
    identical either way (soundness check)."""
    base, afters, unrelated, schedule = build_planted_scenario(
        n_conflict_regions=n_conflict_regions, n_unrelated=n_unrelated)
    step_u, eager_u, coord_u = _run_schedule(base, afters, schedule, unrelated, use_bounds=False)
    step_b, eager_b, coord_b = _run_schedule(base, afters, schedule, unrelated, use_bounds=True)
    from eico.projection.python import unproject
    merged_u = unproject(coord_u.cur)
    merged_b = unproject(coord_b.cur)
    return ComponentCloseMeasurement(
        label=label or f"planted-{len(afters)}",
        n_agents=len(afters), unrelated_agents=unrelated,
        close_step_unbounded=step_u, close_step_bounded=step_b,
        eager_admits_unbounded=eager_u, eager_admits_bounded=eager_b,
        merged_identical=(merged_u == merged_b),
        closed_earlier=(step_b < step_u))

"""U7 — the GATE for U8 (plan 2026-07-31-001, R11).

Two measurements, taken on U11's contention-tiered corpus BEFORE the U8 scheduler is built,
that together decide whether an interaction-uncertainty scheduler is worth building:

  (a) **commute-class entropy vs observed conflict.** For a cell with K candidate edit variants
      (sampled from the model) and a FIXED neighbour edit, partition the variants into
      *commute classes* by how each commutes with the neighbour under the cell law
      (`eico.cells.clashing_cells`): two variants are in the same class iff they clash with the
      neighbour on exactly the same cells (the empty signature = commutes cleanly). The Shannon
      entropy of that partition is the cell's commute-class entropy. If entropy tracks the
      observed conflict rate across cells, a scheduler can PREDICT contention from the sampled
      spread instead of waiting for the collision.

  (b) **predictive footprints at N>2** (`kernel.harness.footprints.measure_component_close`):
      whether declared bounds change an observable at scale — an unrelated component closing
      earlier — which the 2-agent single-conflict case structurally cannot show.

`gate_decision` combines them into a go/no-go. The plan's rule, verbatim: pass = entropy
correlates AND/OR predictive footprints change outcomes at scale; fail = record the honest
negative and set U8 to degrade to pi/C-only. The empirical pass/fail ON THE REAL CORPUS is
DATA, reported in the eval — this module and its test certify the harness COMPUTES the two
measurements and combines them by the rule, not that the real corpus happens to pass.

Multi-sample access: the entropy in (a) needs K samples per cell. Per memory
`agent-eval-litellm-proxy` the LiteLLM proxy does not reliably expose logprobs, so `probe_sample_access`
defaults to a sampling fallback and RECORDS the cost (K model calls per cell) rather than
assuming free logprob access; a `sampler` is injectable so the harness (and its test) run
offline.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import math
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from eico.cells import clashing_cells
from eico.projection.python import project
from kernel.lift.lift import lift_file


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# (a) commute-class entropy
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
@dataclass
class EntropyMeasurement:
    cell: str
    n_variants: int
    n_classes: int
    entropy_bits: float
    conflict_rate: float                       # fraction of variants that clash with the neighbour
    classes: dict = field(default_factory=dict)  # class signature (tuple) -> variant count


def _entropy_bits(counts) -> float:
    total = sum(counts)
    if total <= 0:
        return 0.0
    h = 0.0
    for c in counts:
        if c > 0:
            p = c / total
            h -= p * math.log2(p)
    return h


def commute_class(art, variant_effects, neighbour_effects) -> tuple:
    """The commute-class signature of one variant against a fixed neighbour: the sorted union
    of clashing cells across every (variant-effect, neighbour-effect) pair. Empty = the variant
    commutes cleanly with the neighbour. Two variants with the same signature are in one class."""
    clash: set[str] = set()
    for ev in variant_effects:
        for en in neighbour_effects:
            clash.update(clashing_cells(art, ev, en))
    return tuple(sorted(clash))


def measure_cell_entropy(base: str, variant_afters, neighbour_after: str, *,
                         cell: str = "", neighbour_agent: str = "N") -> EntropyMeasurement:
    """Lift each variant `after` and the neighbour `after` against the shared `base`, group the
    variants into commute classes against the neighbour, and report the class-partition entropy
    plus the fraction of variants that clash (non-empty signature)."""
    art = project(base)
    neighbour = lift_file(base, neighbour_after, agent=neighbour_agent).eico_effects()
    classes: dict[tuple, int] = {}
    n_conflict = 0
    for i, after in enumerate(variant_afters):
        eff = lift_file(base, after, agent=f"V{i}").eico_effects()
        sig = commute_class(art, eff, neighbour)
        classes[sig] = classes.get(sig, 0) + 1
        if sig:
            n_conflict += 1
    n = len(variant_afters)
    return EntropyMeasurement(
        cell=cell, n_variants=n, n_classes=len(classes),
        entropy_bits=_entropy_bits(list(classes.values())),
        conflict_rate=(n_conflict / n if n else 0.0), classes=classes)


def _spearman(xs, ys) -> float:
    """Spearman rank correlation with average-rank tie handling. Returns 0.0 for <2 points or a
    constant series (no monotone signal to detect)."""
    n = len(xs)
    if n < 2:
        return 0.0

    def ranks(vals):
        order = sorted(range(n), key=lambda i: vals[i])
        r = [0.0] * n
        i = 0
        while i < n:
            j = i
            while j + 1 < n and vals[order[j + 1]] == vals[order[i]]:
                j += 1
            avg = (i + j) / 2 + 1  # average rank (1-based) of the tie block
            for k in range(i, j + 1):
                r[order[k]] = avg
            i = j + 1
        return r

    rx, ry = ranks(xs), ranks(ys)
    mx, my = sum(rx) / n, sum(ry) / n
    num = sum((rx[i] - mx) * (ry[i] - my) for i in range(n))
    dx = math.sqrt(sum((rx[i] - mx) ** 2 for i in range(n)))
    dy = math.sqrt(sum((ry[i] - my) ** 2 for i in range(n)))
    if dx == 0 or dy == 0:
        return 0.0
    return num / (dx * dy)


def calibration_curve(measurements) -> list[tuple[float, float]]:
    """The (commute-class entropy, observed conflict rate) pairs across cells — the curve the
    plan reports. Sorted by entropy so a monotone trend is legible."""
    return sorted((m.entropy_bits, m.conflict_rate) for m in measurements)


def entropy_conflict_correlation(measurements) -> float:
    """Spearman rank correlation between commute-class entropy and observed conflict rate across
    the measured cells. This is the (a) signal `gate_decision` thresholds."""
    return _spearman([m.entropy_bits for m in measurements],
                     [m.conflict_rate for m in measurements])


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# multi-sample access (scenario 4)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
@dataclass
class SampleAccess:
    logprobs_available: bool
    mode: str            # "logprob" | "sampling"
    samples_drawn: int
    cost_calls: int      # model calls spent to obtain the variant spread (recorded, not hidden)
    variants: list = field(default_factory=list)


def probe_sample_access(*, k: int = 8, sampler=None, logprob_probe=None) -> SampleAccess:
    """Determine how the commute-class variant spread is obtained. `logprob_probe()` reports
    whether the proxy exposes per-token logprobs (a single-call entropy estimate); it defaults
    to False, matching the LiteLLM proxy reality (memory `agent-eval-litellm-proxy`). When
    logprobs are unavailable the harness falls back to drawing `k` independent samples via
    `sampler(k)` and records the cost as `k` calls. Offline (no sampler) yields a zero-cost,
    zero-sample sampling record so the harness never blocks CI."""
    available = bool(logprob_probe()) if logprob_probe is not None else False
    if available:
        return SampleAccess(logprobs_available=True, mode="logprob",
                            samples_drawn=1, cost_calls=1)
    variants = list(sampler(k)) if sampler is not None else []
    return SampleAccess(logprobs_available=False, mode="sampling",
                        samples_drawn=len(variants), cost_calls=len(variants),
                        variants=variants)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# the gate
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
@dataclass
class GateVerdict:
    entropy_correlates: bool
    footprints_change_outcomes: bool
    correlation: float
    decision: str        # "go" | "no-go"
    rationale: str


def gate_decision(entropy_measurements, close_measurements, *,
                  corr_threshold: float = 0.5) -> GateVerdict:
    """Combine the two U7 signals into a go/no-go for U8. `go` iff commute-class entropy
    correlates with observed conflict (Spearman >= `corr_threshold`) OR declared bounds change
    an outcome at scale (some unrelated component closes earlier under bounds). `no-go` records
    the honest negative and tells U8 to degrade to pi/C-only."""
    corr = entropy_conflict_correlation(entropy_measurements)
    entropy_ok = corr >= corr_threshold
    footprints_ok = any(m.closed_earlier for m in close_measurements)
    go = entropy_ok or footprints_ok
    bits = []
    if entropy_ok:
        bits.append(f"entropy~conflict Spearman={corr:.2f}>={corr_threshold}")
    else:
        bits.append(f"entropy~conflict Spearman={corr:.2f}<{corr_threshold}")
    bits.append("bounds close an unrelated component earlier at N>2"
                if footprints_ok else "bounds change no outcome at N>2")
    return GateVerdict(
        entropy_correlates=entropy_ok, footprints_change_outcomes=footprints_ok,
        correlation=corr, decision="go" if go else "no-go",
        rationale="; ".join(bits) + (
            "" if go else " -> U8 degrades to pi/C-only"))

"""U8 — the interaction-uncertainty scheduler (plan 2026-07-31-001, R9/R10).

Built because U7's gate returned GO (predictive-footprint arm: at N>2 an unrelated component
closes earlier under declared bounds; see `kernel.harness.footprints.measure_component_close`).
The scheduler partitions the co-edited regions of a shared artifact into an EAGER SKELETON —
the regions worth coordinating first, whose committed values become fixed inputs the rest react
to — and SPECULATIVE HOLES, filled concurrently via U5's reactive dispatch. Raising the fraction
of regions that fill speculatively is exactly raising the effective parallel fraction `p`.

The decision quantities (plan §Approach):

  pi(r)   interaction probability. Grounded in the substrate: r interacts with r' iff their
          PREDICTED edits `may_interact` under the cell law + footprint overlap
          (`eico.commutativity_algebra.may_interact`, the same predicate the streaming
          Coordinator uses to decide what resolves jointly). pi(r) is the fraction of the other
          regions r STILL contends with. It is computed DYNAMICALLY: once a region is coordinated
          its value is fixed, so it stops being a live source of contention for its neighbours and
          their pi drops — this is what lets the skeleton stay small.

  C(r)    compatibility: P(two concurrent edits to r commute) in [0,1], from the ONE shared
          sampling pass (U7's variant spread). High C = the sampled edits agree, so a collision,
          if it happens, resolves cleanly and cheaply.

  U_i(r)  the sampled commute-class entropy from U7 (`EntropyMeasurement.entropy_bits`). Reported,
          and — only when U7 passed — used to break ties in the greedy refinement (coordinate the
          more UNCERTAIN of two equally-hazardous regions first, since its collision is the harder
          one to predict).

  Haz(r) = pi(r) * (1 - C(r))                      high interaction AND low compatibility
  decision: coordinate r first iff Haz(r) > tau,   tau = C_coord / C_repair

`tau` is the coordination/repair cost ratio: coordinating is worth it exactly when the expected
repair cost it avoids (Haz(r) * C_repair) exceeds the coordination cost (C_coord), i.e. when
Haz(r) > C_coord/C_repair. Cheap coordination (small tau) lowers the bar; cheap repair (large
tau) raises it.

Degrade mode: if U7 had returned no-go, the entropy/uncertainty signal is not trusted, so the
scheduler runs `pi`/`C`-only — a STATIC hazard threshold with no sequential recomputation and no
uncertainty tie-break — and the schedule is flagged `degraded=True` so the report says so. The
full mode's sequential VoI refinement (fix the worst region, recompute everyone's pi, repeat) is
what U7's go verdict buys.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from eico.commutativity_algebra import may_interact
from eico.projection.python import project
from kernel.lift.lift import lift_file


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# per-region signals
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
@dataclass
class RegionInput:
    """One co-edited region of the shared artifact. `interacts_with` is the substrate-computed
    set of OTHER region names whose predicted edits `may_interact` with this one (built by
    `interaction_graph`, or supplied directly in a test). `compatibility` is C(r) and
    `uncertainty` is U_i(r), both from the one shared sampling pass."""
    name: str
    interacts_with: frozenset = frozenset()
    compatibility: float = 1.0     # C(r): P(concurrent edits commute); 1.0 = always compatible
    uncertainty: float = 0.0       # U_i(r): sampled commute-class entropy bits (U7)


@dataclass
class RegionDecision:
    name: str
    role: str          # "skeleton" (coordinate first) | "speculative" (fill concurrently)
    pi: float          # interaction probability at the moment the decision was taken
    compatibility: float
    hazard: float
    order: int         # coordination order within the skeleton (0-based); -1 for speculative


@dataclass
class Schedule:
    decisions: list             # list[RegionDecision], skeleton first (in coordination order)
    tau: float
    mode: str                   # "full" | "pi-C-only"
    degraded: bool
    rationale: str
    skeleton: list = field(default_factory=list)     # region names, coordination order
    speculative: list = field(default_factory=list)  # region names

    @property
    def speculative_fraction(self) -> float:
        """The effective parallel fraction `p` the scheduler exposes: regions that fill
        concurrently instead of being serialized into the coordinated skeleton."""
        n = len(self.decisions)
        return len(self.speculative) / n if n else 0.0


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# substrate-grounded interaction graph (pi's source)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def interaction_graph(base: str, predicted_afters: dict) -> dict:
    """Build the region interaction graph from REAL predicted edits. `predicted_afters` maps a
    region name to its representative predicted `after` text (the seed edit / a sampled variant).
    Two regions interact iff any pair of their lifted effects `may_interact` under the cell law —
    the identical predicate `eico.streaming.Coordinator` uses to decide joint resolution, so the
    graph the scheduler reasons over is the one the coordinator will actually enforce.

    Returns `{region_name: frozenset(other names it interacts with)}`."""
    art = project(base)
    effects = {
        name: lift_file(base, after, agent=name).eico_effects()
        for name, after in predicted_afters.items()
    }
    names = list(predicted_afters)
    graph = {name: set() for name in names}
    for i in range(len(names)):
        for j in range(i + 1, len(names)):
            a, b = names[i], names[j]
            if any(may_interact(art, e1, e2) for e1 in effects[a] for e2 in effects[b]):
                graph[a].add(b)
                graph[b].add(a)
    return {k: frozenset(v) for k, v in graph.items()}


def regions_from_edits(base: str, predicted_afters: dict, *,
                       compatibility: dict = None, uncertainty: dict = None) -> list:
    """Convenience: build `RegionInput`s from real predicted edits, wiring `interacts_with` from
    the substrate graph and taking C(r)/U_i(r) from the (optional) sampling-pass maps (default
    C=1.0 fully compatible, U=0.0 — the no-contention prior)."""
    graph = interaction_graph(base, predicted_afters)
    compatibility = compatibility or {}
    uncertainty = uncertainty or {}
    return [
        RegionInput(name=name, interacts_with=graph[name],
                    compatibility=compatibility.get(name, 1.0),
                    uncertainty=uncertainty.get(name, 0.0))
        for name in predicted_afters
    ]


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# the scheduler
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def schedule_regions(regions, *, c_coord: float = 1.0, c_repair: float = 4.0,
                     u7_passed: bool = True) -> Schedule:
    """Partition `regions` into an eager skeleton and speculative holes.

    tau = c_coord / c_repair is the hazard threshold above which coordinating a region first is
    cheaper in expectation than repairing its collision later.

    full mode (u7_passed): sequential VoI greedy. Repeatedly take the live region of maximum
    hazard whose Haz > tau, move it into the skeleton, and FIX it — which removes it from its
    neighbours' live interaction sets, lowering their pi. Fixing the worst region can drop a
    neighbour below tau, so the skeleton stays as small as the contention truly requires and the
    rest fill speculatively. Ties broken by higher uncertainty (U_i), then name (deterministic).

    pi/C-only mode (not u7_passed): a STATIC threshold on the initial hazard — no sequential
    recomputation, no uncertainty tie-break — and `degraded=True` so the report states it.
    """
    tau = c_coord / c_repair
    by_name = {r.name: r for r in regions}
    names = [r.name for r in regions]
    n = len(names)
    denom = max(n - 1, 1)  # a region's pi is measured against the other regions

    def pi_of(name, live: set) -> float:
        # live sources of contention: interacting regions not yet coordinated (still un-fixed).
        contenders = by_name[name].interacts_with & (live - {name})
        return len(contenders) / denom

    def hazard_of(name, live: set) -> float:
        return pi_of(name, live) * (1.0 - by_name[name].compatibility)

    skeleton: list = []
    decisions_by_name: dict = {}

    if u7_passed:
        live = set(names)
        order = 0
        while True:
            # candidates still live and over threshold, ranked by (hazard, uncertainty, name).
            ranked = sorted(
                (nm for nm in live if hazard_of(nm, live) > tau),
                key=lambda nm: (hazard_of(nm, live), by_name[nm].uncertainty, nm),
                reverse=True,
            )
            if not ranked:
                break
            pick = ranked[0]
            decisions_by_name[pick] = RegionDecision(
                name=pick, role="skeleton", pi=pi_of(pick, live),
                compatibility=by_name[pick].compatibility,
                hazard=hazard_of(pick, live), order=order)
            skeleton.append(pick)
            live.discard(pick)  # fixing it lowers every neighbour's pi on the next pass
            order += 1
        mode, degraded = "full", False
    else:
        live = set(names)  # static: no region is ever fixed, so pi never drops
        selected = [nm for nm in names if hazard_of(nm, live) > tau]
        selected.sort(key=lambda nm: (hazard_of(nm, live), nm), reverse=True)
        for order, nm in enumerate(selected):
            decisions_by_name[nm] = RegionDecision(
                name=nm, role="skeleton", pi=pi_of(nm, live),
                compatibility=by_name[nm].compatibility,
                hazard=hazard_of(nm, live), order=order)
        skeleton = selected
        mode, degraded = "pi-C-only", True

    speculative = [nm for nm in names if nm not in decisions_by_name]
    live_final = {nm for nm in names if nm not in skeleton} if u7_passed else set(names)
    for nm in speculative:
        decisions_by_name[nm] = RegionDecision(
            name=nm, role="speculative", pi=pi_of(nm, live_final),
            compatibility=by_name[nm].compatibility,
            hazard=hazard_of(nm, live_final), order=-1)

    decisions = [decisions_by_name[nm] for nm in skeleton] + \
                [decisions_by_name[nm] for nm in speculative]

    rationale = (
        f"tau=C_coord/C_repair={c_coord:g}/{c_repair:g}={tau:.3f}; "
        f"{len(skeleton)}/{n} coordinated (skeleton), {len(speculative)}/{n} speculative; "
        f"mode={mode}"
        + ("" if u7_passed else "; U7 no-go -> pi/C-only, uncertainty signal dropped (degraded)"))
    return Schedule(decisions=decisions, tau=tau, mode=mode, degraded=degraded,
                    rationale=rationale, skeleton=skeleton, speculative=speculative)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# ablation: scheduler disabled (the U8 contribution isolator, plan scenario 4)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def naive_schedule(regions) -> Schedule:
    """The scheduler-DISABLED baseline: no hazard prioritization, no sequential fixing — every
    region that has ANY predicted interaction is coordinated (conservative serialization), only
    fully-disjoint regions fill speculatively. On a fan-out with one hot spot this over-
    coordinates the hot spot's neighbours that the full scheduler would let react, so its
    `speculative_fraction` (effective p) is lower — isolating the scheduler's contribution."""
    names = [r.name for r in regions]
    n = len(names)
    denom = max(n - 1, 1)
    skeleton = [r.name for r in regions if r.interacts_with]
    speculative = [r.name for r in regions if not r.interacts_with]
    decisions = []
    for order, r in enumerate(regions):
        interacting = bool(r.interacts_with)
        decisions.append(RegionDecision(
            name=r.name, role="skeleton" if interacting else "speculative",
            pi=len(r.interacts_with) / denom, compatibility=r.compatibility,
            hazard=(len(r.interacts_with) / denom) * (1.0 - r.compatibility),
            order=(skeleton.index(r.name) if interacting else -1)))
    return Schedule(
        decisions=decisions, tau=float("nan"), mode="disabled", degraded=False,
        rationale=f"scheduler disabled: {len(skeleton)}/{n} coordinated (any interaction), "
                  f"{len(speculative)}/{n} speculative",
        skeleton=skeleton, speculative=speculative)

"""U8 — the interaction-uncertainty scheduler (plan 2026-07-31-001, R9/R10).

Scenarios (from the plan, verbatim):
  (1) a high-contention / low-compatibility region lands in the eager skeleton (coordinate first);
  (2) a disjoint low-hazard region fills speculatively (concurrent);
  (3) with U7 marked FAIL the scheduler runs pi/C-only and the schedule flags degradation;
  (4) the ablation — scheduler disabled shows a LOWER effective p (speculative fraction) than the
      full reactive scheduler on a fan-out task, isolating the scheduler's contribution.

pi is grounded in the substrate (`may_interact` on lifted predicted edits); C(r)/U_i(r) are the
sampling-pass inputs. The threshold is tau = C_coord / C_repair.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import pytest

from kernel.scheduler import hazard as hz


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# substrate grounding: the interaction graph is computed from REAL edits
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def test_interaction_graph_is_computed_from_real_footprints():
    # a.py-style single file: two agents rewrite the SAME function body (contend); a third
    # rewrites a disjoint function (independent).
    base = "def hot(x):\n    return x + 1\n\n\ndef cold(y):\n    return y + 1\n"
    predicted = {
        "A": "def hot(x):\n    return x + 2\n\n\ndef cold(y):\n    return y + 1\n",
        "B": "def hot(x):\n    return x + 3\n\n\ndef cold(y):\n    return y + 1\n",
        "C": "def hot(x):\n    return x + 1\n\n\ndef cold(y):\n    return y + 9\n",
    }
    graph = hz.interaction_graph(base, predicted)
    assert graph["A"] == frozenset({"B"})   # A and B contend on hot()
    assert graph["B"] == frozenset({"A"})
    assert graph["C"] == frozenset()         # C is disjoint


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# scenario 1: high-contention / low-compatibility region -> eager skeleton
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def test_high_hazard_region_lands_in_skeleton():
    regions = [
        hz.RegionInput("hot", interacts_with=frozenset({"n1", "n2"}), compatibility=0.0),
        hz.RegionInput("n1", interacts_with=frozenset({"hot"}), compatibility=0.9),
        hz.RegionInput("n2", interacts_with=frozenset({"hot"}), compatibility=0.9),
    ]
    sched = hz.schedule_regions(regions, c_coord=1.0, c_repair=4.0)
    # hot: pi = 2/2 = 1.0, C = 0 -> Haz = 1.0 > tau = 0.25 -> coordinate first.
    assert "hot" in sched.skeleton
    assert sched.skeleton[0] == "hot"
    hot = next(d for d in sched.decisions if d.name == "hot")
    assert hot.role == "skeleton"
    assert hot.hazard > sched.tau


def test_fixing_the_hot_region_drops_neighbours_below_threshold():
    # the sequential-VoI payoff: coordinating `hot` fixes its value, so n1/n2 stop contending and
    # their pi -> 0, dropping them out of the skeleton even though they touch a contended region.
    regions = [

"""U9 — steelmanned baseline arms for the head-to-head (plan 2026-07-31-001, R12).

Each arm is a MERGE POLICY over the same shared agent drafts (a task's `coupling_probe`): the
agents do identical work under one model/temperature/tool config, and the arms differ ONLY in how
the concurrent per-file drafts are reconciled into a committed artifact. That is the harness
discipline the eval rests on — a difference between arms is a difference in reconciliation, never
in the underlying agent work.

  - `concurrent-LWW`  (arms.lww)  file-level last-writer-wins: the last writer's whole file is
    committed, silently dropping every other agent's edit — the corruption null we must reject.
  - `concurrent-CRDT` (arms.crdt) AST-node LWW-register: order-INSENSITIVE convergence with a
    fixed replica-id tiebreak. Always "clean" (never reports a conflict), merges disjoint edits
    correctly, but on a true same-node conflict it silently keeps one side — clean yet corrupt.
  - `concurrent-MTPO` (arms.mtpo) static launch-time serialization: sequential fold in launch
    order, last-in-order wins per node — order-SENSITIVE by construction (CoAgent mechanism).
"""
from experiments.agent_eval.arms.base import ArmConfig, ArmResult, input_digest, run_all_arms
from experiments.agent_eval.arms.crdt import crdt_arm, crdt_merge
from experiments.agent_eval.arms.lww import lww_arm, lww_merge
from experiments.agent_eval.arms.mtpo import mtpo_arm, mtpo_merge

__all__ = [
    "ArmConfig", "ArmResult", "input_digest", "run_all_arms",
    "lww_arm", "lww_merge", "crdt_arm", "crdt_merge", "mtpo_arm", "mtpo_merge",
]

"""Shared arm protocol + the harness-discipline check (plan 2026-07-31-001, R12).

An arm consumes a task's per-file agent drafts (`coupling_probe`: path -> tuple[AgentEdit]) plus
that file's base (`files[path]`) and returns an `ArmResult` — the committed artifact per file, and
what the merge policy did to get there (dropped edits, clean/conflict, order sensitivity).

`run_all_arms` runs every arm on ONE task under ONE `ArmConfig` and stamps each result with the
same `input_digest`, so the eval can assert every arm reconciled the IDENTICAL agent work under
the IDENTICAL model/temperature/tools — the discipline that makes an arm-to-arm difference a
difference in reconciliation, not in the agents.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
from dataclasses import dataclass, field


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ArmConfig:
    """The single model/temperature/tool configuration under which every arm's agent drafts were
    produced. Shared across arms verbatim (R12 scenario 4)."""
    model: str = "gpt-5.5"
    temperature: float = 0.0
    tools: tuple = ("read_file", "write_file")


@dataclass
class ArmResult:
    arm: str
    files: dict                     # committed artifact: path -> merged text
    clean: bool                     # did the policy complete without reporting a conflict?
    dropped_edits: list = field(default_factory=list)   # (agent, path) edits silently lost
    order_sensitive: bool = False   # does the committed artifact depend on launch order?
    config: ArmConfig = field(default_factory=ArmConfig)
    input_digest: str = ""          # hash of (shared agent drafts + config); identical across arms
    notes: str = ""


def _edits_for(task):
    """The per-file agent drafts an arm reconciles: `coupling_probe` when present (the isolated
    per-agent drafts the tiers pre-register), else the single-author `gold_files`/`files` fallback
    so control tasks still run through the arms."""
    if getattr(task, "coupling_probe", None):
        return dict(task.coupling_probe)
    return {}


def input_digest(task, config: ArmConfig) -> str:
    """A stable hash of the SHARED inputs every arm sees: each file's base, the ordered agent
    drafts, and the config. Two arms with the same digest provably reconciled identical work."""
    edits = _edits_for(task)
    payload = {
        "files": {p: task.files.get(p, "") for p in edits},
        "edits": {p: [(e.agent, e.after) for e in aes] for p, aes in sorted(edits.items())},
        "config": [config.model, config.temperature, list(config.tools)],
    }
    blob = json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True).encode()
    return hashlib.sha256(blob).hexdigest()[:16]


def run_all_arms(task, arms, *, config: ArmConfig = None, order=None) -> dict:
    """Run every arm in `arms` (name -> callable(task, config, order)) on `task` under one shared
    `config`, stamping each result with the shared `input_digest`. Returns {arm_name: ArmResult}."""
    config = config or ArmConfig()
    digest = input_digest(task, config)
    out = {}
    for name, fn in arms.items():
        res = fn(task, config=config, order=order)
        res.input_digest = digest
        out[name] = res
    return out

"""`concurrent-LWW` — file-level last-writer-wins (plan 2026-07-31-001, R12).

The coarsest concurrent baseline: agents write the whole file; the last writer's file is
committed and every other writer's edit is silently discarded. On a T0 disjoint fan-out (one agent
per file) this is lossless. On ANY file two agents co-edit — even disjoint symbols (T1) — it
silently overwrites one agent's work. That silent overwrite is the corruption null the eval must
be able to reject.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from experiments.agent_eval.arms.base import ArmConfig, ArmResult, _edits_for


def _order_key(edits, order):
    names = order if order is not None else [e.agent for e in edits]
    return lambda e: (names.index(e.agent) if e.agent in names else len(names), e.agent)


def lww_merge(base: str, edits, order=None) -> tuple[str, list]:
    """Return `(committed_text, dropped_agents)` for one file. The last writer in launch order
    wins the whole file; all earlier writers whose draft differs are dropped."""
    if not edits:
        return base, []
    ordered = sorted(edits, key=_order_key(edits, order))
    winner = ordered[-1]
    dropped = [e.agent for e in ordered[:-1] if e.after != winner.after]
    return winner.after, dropped


def lww_arm(task, *, config: ArmConfig = None, order=None) -> ArmResult:
    edits_by_file = _edits_for(task)
    files, dropped = {}, []
    for path, edits in edits_by_file.items():
        merged, dropped_agents = lww_merge(task.files.get(path, ""), edits, order)
        files[path] = merged
        dropped += [(a, path) for a in dropped_agents]
    return ArmResult(
        arm="concurrent-LWW", files=files, clean=True, dropped_edits=dropped,
        # last-writer-wins is order-sensitive whenever >1 agent co-edits a file.
        order_sensitive=any(len(e) > 1 for e in edits_by_file.values()),
        config=config or ArmConfig(),
        notes="file-level last-writer-wins; dropped edits are silent (no conflict reported)")

"""`concurrent-CRDT` — AST-node LWW-register merge (plan 2026-07-31-001, R12).

The nearest defensible port of a CodeCRDT-class mechanism at AST-node granularity (the fairness
rule from the COLM design: match EICO's cell granularity so the comparison isn't rigged by giving
the CRDT a coarser view). Each top-level entity is a last-writer-wins register keyed by a FIXED
replica id (agent name), so the merge is:

  - **convergent / order-insensitive** — the committed artifact is independent of the order the
    concurrent drafts arrive in (the defining CRDT property);
  - **always "clean"** — it never reports a conflict; a divergent same-entity edit is resolved by
    the replica-id tiebreak, not surfaced;
  - **correct on disjoint edits** — two agents editing different entities (T1 shared-read) both
    land, where file-level LWW would drop one;
  - **silently lossy on a true conflict** — two agents editing the SAME entity differently (T2
    shared signature) keep only the tiebreak winner, so a required parameter is dropped: the merge
    is clean and syntactically valid yet semantically wrong. That gap is what the U10 oracle catches.

No commute law, no invariant gate — a CRDT guarantees convergence, not semantic correctness.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from experiments.agent_eval.arms.base import ArmConfig, ArmResult, _edits_for
from eico.artifact import Artifact, Node
from eico.projection.python import project, render


def crdt_merge(base: str, edits) -> tuple[str, list, bool]:
    """Return `(committed_text, dropped, clean)` for one file. `dropped` is the list of
    `(agent, entity)` contributions overridden by the replica-id tiebreak on a same-entity
    conflict. `clean` is always True: a CRDT converges rather than conflicting."""
    if not edits:
        return base, [], True
    base_art = project(base)
    base_children = base_art.root.children

    # per entity: the (agent, node) sides that changed it away from base.
    changed: dict[str, list] = {}
    for e in edits:
        art = project(e.after)
        for key in set(base_children) | set(art.root.children):
            node = art.root.children.get(key)
            if node != base_children.get(key):
                changed.setdefault(key, []).append((e.agent, node))

    merged = dict(base_children)
    dropped: list = []
    for key, sides in changed.items():
        distinct: list = []                       # (agent, node), de-duped by node value
        for agent, node in sides:
            if not any(node == d[1] for d in distinct):
                distinct.append((agent, node))
        winner = min(distinct, key=lambda an: an[0])   # fixed replica-id tiebreak -> convergent
        if winner[1] is None:
            merged.pop(key, None)
        else:
            merged[key] = winner[1]
        for agent, _node in distinct:
            if agent != winner[0]:
                dropped.append((agent, key))
    text = render(Artifact(Node("record", children=merged, ordered=base_art.root.ordered)))
    return text, dropped, True


def crdt_arm(task, *, config: ArmConfig = None, order=None) -> ArmResult:
    # order is accepted for a uniform arm signature but IGNORED: CRDT is order-insensitive.
    edits_by_file = _edits_for(task)
    files, dropped = {}, []
    for path, edits in edits_by_file.items():
        merged, dropped_pairs, _clean = crdt_merge(task.files.get(path, ""), edits)
        files[path] = merged
        dropped += [(a, path) for a, _entity in dropped_pairs]
    return ArmResult(
        arm="concurrent-CRDT", files=files, clean=True, dropped_edits=dropped,
        order_sensitive=False, config=config or ArmConfig(),
        notes="AST-node LWW-register; convergent + always clean; lossy on same-entity conflicts")

"""`concurrent-MTPO` — static launch-time serialization (plan 2026-07-31-001, R12, R-positioning).

The CoAgent/MTPO mechanism (Lyu et al., arXiv:2508.xxxxx): agents are ordered at LAUNCH time; each
agent's result is notified one-way to the next, which re-judges on top. The committed artifact is a
sequential fold in launch order — last-in-order wins per entity. Serializable at quiescence, but
order-SENSITIVE by construction: a different launch order can commit a different artifact whenever
two agents contend on one entity. That order sensitivity is the contrast with EICO's H2
(schedule-independent commit); the eval measures it directly (U10 schedule-independence harness).

Modeling note (deviation, logged): the "LLM re-judge" step is stubbed by the deterministic
last-in-order override. Each agent's change set is taken relative to `base` and applied in order,
so a later agent's edit to an entity supersedes an earlier one — which is exactly what a re-judge
that trusts the most recent notified state produces, without a live model (OpenAI out of quota,
memory `agent-eval-litellm-proxy`). Disjoint edits are order-insensitive (both land); only true
contention exposes the order sensitivity.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from experiments.agent_eval.arms.base import ArmConfig, ArmResult, _edits_for
from eico.artifact import Artifact, Node
from eico.projection.python import project, render


def _launch_order(edits, order):
    names = order if order is not None else [e.agent for e in edits]
    return sorted(edits, key=lambda e: (names.index(e.agent) if e.agent in names else len(names),
                                        e.agent))


def mtpo_merge(base: str, edits, order=None) -> tuple[str, list]:
    """Return `(committed_text, superseded)` for one file. Agents apply in launch order; a later
    agent's edit to an entity supersedes an earlier one. `superseded` lists `(agent, entity)`
    contributions overwritten by a later writer in the order."""
    if not edits:
        return base, []
    base_art = project(base)
    base_children = base_art.root.children
    merged = dict(base_children)
    last_writer: dict[str, str] = {}   # entity -> agent that last wrote it (for supersede tracking)
    superseded: list = []
    for e in _launch_order(edits, order):
        art = project(e.after)
        for key in set(base_children) | set(art.root.children):
            node = art.root.children.get(key)
            if node != base_children.get(key):
                if key in last_writer and merged.get(key) != node:
                    superseded.append((last_writer[key], key))
                if node is None:
                    merged.pop(key, None)
                else:
                    merged[key] = node
                last_writer[key] = e.agent
    text = render(Artifact(Node("record", children=merged, ordered=base_art.root.ordered)))
    return text, superseded


def mtpo_arm(task, *, config: ArmConfig = None, order=None) -> ArmResult:
    edits_by_file = _edits_for(task)
    files, superseded = {}, []
    contended = False
    for path, edits in edits_by_file.items():
        merged, sup = mtpo_merge(task.files.get(path, ""), edits, order)
        files[path] = merged
        superseded += [(a, path) for a, _entity in sup]
        if sup:
            contended = True
    return ArmResult(
        arm="concurrent-MTPO", files=files, clean=True, dropped_edits=superseded,
        order_sensitive=contended,  # a superseded entity is where launch order changes the commit
        config=config or ArmConfig(),
        notes="static launch-order serialization; last-in-order wins per entity (re-judge stubbed)")

"""U9 — steelmanned baseline arms LWW / CRDT / MTPO (plan 2026-07-31-001, R12).

Scenarios (from the plan, verbatim):
  (1) LWW on a T2 shared-write task silently overwrites one agent's edit (the corruption null we
      must be able to reject);
  (2) CRDT merges cleanly on T2 yet is semantically wrong at a measurable rate (a required param
      is dropped) — while merging a T1 disjoint co-edit correctly;
  (3) MTPO's static pre-order produces a DIFFERENT committed artifact under two launch orders
      (order-sensitivity by construction), contrasting with EICO's H2;
  (4) all arms run on the same model/temperature/tools and reconcile the IDENTICAL agent drafts
      (harness discipline) — asserted via a shared input digest.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from experiments.agent_eval.arms import (
    ArmConfig, crdt_arm, lww_arm, mtpo_arm, run_all_arms)
from experiments.agent_eval.corpus.migration import (
    disjoint_fanout_task, interdependent_ripple_task, shared_read_task, shared_signature_task)

# scenario 1: LWW silently overwrites on a shared-write task

def test_lww_silently_overwrites_a_shared_write():
    task = shared_signature_task()  # T2: A adds timeout, B adds retries onto request()
    res = lww_arm(task, config=ArmConfig())
    committed = res.files["client.py"]
    edits = {e.agent: e.after for e in task.coupling_probe["client.py"]}
    # the whole file is exactly ONE agent's draft; the other agent's edit is gone.
    assert committed in (edits["A"], edits["B"])
    assert res.dropped_edits, "LWW must record the silently dropped agent"
    assert res.clean is True  # no conflict is EVER reported -- that is the danger
    # corruption is real: the committed file is not the gold two-param signature.
    assert committed != task.gold_files["client.py"]


def test_lww_drops_a_disjoint_coedit_too():
    # even on T1 where the two agents touch DISJOINT symbols, file-level LWW drops one whole draft.
    task = shared_read_task()
    res = lww_arm(task, config=ArmConfig())
    assert res.dropped_edits
    assert res.files["rates.py"] != task.gold_files["rates.py"]

# scenario 2: CRDT merges cleanly on T2 yet is semantically wrong; correct on T1

def test_crdt_merges_cleanly_but_is_corrupt_on_shared_write():
    task = shared_signature_task()
    res = crdt_arm(task, config=ArmConfig())
    assert res.clean is True                       # CRDT never conflicts -- it converges
    committed = res.files["client.py"]
    # a same-entity conflict -> one side's parameter is silently kept, the other dropped.
    assert res.dropped_edits
    assert committed != task.gold_files["client.py"]
    # ...yet it is syntactically valid Python (the corruption is semantic, not a parse error).
    compile(committed, "client.py", "exec")


def test_crdt_is_correct_on_a_disjoint_coedit():
    # the fairness point: at AST-node granularity CRDT lands BOTH disjoint symbol edits (T1),
    # where file-level LWW drops one. This is why CRDT is the steelman, not a strawman.
    task = shared_read_task()
    res = crdt_arm(task, config=ArmConfig())
    assert res.clean is True

"""U10 — the semantic-corruption oracle (plan 2026-07-31-001, R13).

The primary SAFETY metric. Corruption is the dangerous failure mode a concurrent editor can hide:
a merge that

    completes cleanly (no conflict reported)  AND
    parses                                     AND
    passes the import/link (type-ish) smoke    AND
    FAILS the semantic oracle (the task's real acceptance tests)

— i.e. it looks done and compiles, but is wrong. A merge that overtly fails to parse or import is
NOT corruption in this sense: it is caught by cheaper gates and is loud, not silent. The whole
point of the metric is to count the SILENT wrongs (a dropped required parameter, an invariant one
agent relied on that another quietly broke), which is exactly what LWW/CRDT produce on contended
tiers (U9) and what EICO's commute-OCC + invariant-confluence gate is meant to refuse.

The semantic stage reuses the existing synthetic grader (`grading.grade_synthetic`): it writes the
committed files + the task's acceptance test into a scratch dir and runs pytest. The import smoke
stands in for the "type check" (this repo has no separate type gate for synthetic tasks; an
import-time run catches the NameError/ImportError class a parse cannot — the same rationale as
`kernel.ladder.smoke`).

`mutation_test` certifies the oracle CATCHES what it claims: it plants known-corrupt mutants of a
task's gold and measures the fraction the oracle flags. An oracle that flags nothing is useless;
this is the guard against that.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import ast
import os
import tempfile
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from experiments.agent_eval.grading import grade_synthetic


@dataclass
class CorruptionVerdict:
    merged_clean: bool     # did the merge policy report a clean (conflict-free) commit?
    parses: bool           # every committed file parses
    imports_ok: bool       # every committed file + the acceptance test import without error
    tests_pass: bool       # the task's real acceptance tests pass (the semantic oracle)
    corrupt: bool          # clean AND parses AND imports AND NOT tests_pass -> a SILENT wrong
    stage: str             # where it stopped: "parse" | "import" | "semantic" | "clean-pass"
    detail: str = ""


def _parses(files: dict) -> tuple[bool, str]:
    for path, text in files.items():
        try:
            ast.parse(text)
        except SyntaxError as exc:
            return False, f"{path}: {exc}"
    return True, ""


def _materialize(task, files: dict, scratch: str):
    for path, text in files.items():
        full = os.path.join(scratch, path)
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(full) or scratch, exist_ok=True)
        with open(full, "w") as fh:
            fh.write(text)


def _semantic(task, files: dict) -> tuple[bool, str]:
    """Run the task's real acceptance test against the committed files in a scratch dir."""
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as scratch:
        _materialize(task, files, scratch)
        result = grade_synthetic(task, scratch)
    return bool(result["passed"]), result.get("output_tail", "")


def evaluate_corruption(task, committed_files: dict, *, merged_clean: bool = True) -> CorruptionVerdict:
    """Classify a committed artifact. `merged_clean` is the arm's own report that it committed
    without surfacing a conflict (LWW/CRDT are always clean; a real conflict-reporting merge would
    pass False). Corruption is only asserted for a CLEAN, parseable, importable commit whose
    semantics are wrong — the silent failure the eval must be able to detect and reject."""
    parses, perr = _parses(committed_files)
    if not parses:
        return CorruptionVerdict(merged_clean, False, False, False, corrupt=False,
                                 stage="parse", detail=perr)
    tests_pass, tail = _semantic(task, committed_files)
    # the synthetic grader's pytest run IS the import+semantic check: a collection/import error
    # surfaces as a non-pass with an import traceback rather than a test assertion.
    imports_ok = tests_pass or ("Error" not in tail.split("\n")[-40:].__str__()
                                if False else _imports_ok(tail, tests_pass))
    corrupt = merged_clean and parses and imports_ok and not tests_pass
    if not imports_ok:
        stage = "import"
    elif not tests_pass:
        stage = "semantic"
    else:
        stage = "clean-pass"
    return CorruptionVerdict(merged_clean, parses, imports_ok, tests_pass,
                             corrupt=corrupt, stage=stage, detail=tail[-600:])


def _imports_ok(tail: str, tests_pass: bool) -> bool:
    """Distinguish an import/collection failure (loud, not corruption) from a semantic test
    failure (the silent wrong). If pytest could not even collect/import, the tail carries an
    import-error signature; otherwise a failure is a genuine assertion failure = semantic."""
    if tests_pass:
        return True
    signatures = ("ModuleNotFoundError", "ImportError", "SyntaxError",
                  "errors during collection", "INTERNALERROR")
    return not any(sig in tail for sig in signatures)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# mutation testing — certify the oracle catches planted corruption
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
@dataclass
class MutationReport:
    n_mutants: int
    n_caught: int
    catch_rate: float
    escaped: list = field(default_factory=list)   # descriptions of mutants the oracle missed


def _plant_mutants(task) -> list[tuple[str, dict]]:
    """Derive corrupt-but-clean mutants from the task's gold: each is the gold with ONE file's
    semantics broken while staying syntactically valid (a dropped parameter, a flipped constant, a
    stubbed body). These are the silent wrongs the oracle must flag as corruption."""
    gold = dict(task.gold_files)
    mutants: list[tuple[str, dict]] = []
    for path, text in gold.items():
        try:
            tree = ast.parse(text)
        except SyntaxError:
            continue
        # mutant A: drop the last parameter of the first def (a migration-ripple corruption).
        m = _mutate_drop_last_param(text, tree)
        if m and m != text:
            files = dict(gold); files[path] = m
            mutants.append((f"{path}:drop-last-param", files))
        # mutant B: replace the first numeric literal (flip a migrated constant).
        m = _mutate_flip_number(text, tree)
        if m and m != text:
            files = dict(gold); files[path] = m
            mutants.append((f"{path}:flip-constant", files))
        # mutant C: stub the first def's body to `return None` (drop the migrated behavior).
        m = _mutate_stub_body(text, tree)
        if m and m != text:
            files = dict(gold); files[path] = m
            mutants.append((f"{path}:stub-body", files))
    return mutants


def _mutate_drop_last_param(text: str, tree: ast.Module):
    for node in ast.walk(tree):
        if isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef) and node.args.args:
            victim = node.args.args.copy()
            victim.pop()
            new = ast.parse(text)
            for n2 in ast.walk(new):
                if isinstance(n2, ast.FunctionDef) and n2.name == node.name:
                    n2.args.args = n2.args.args[:-1]
                    break
            return ast.unparse(new)
    return None


def _mutate_flip_number(text: str, tree: ast.Module):
    for node in ast.walk(tree):
        if isinstance(node, ast.Constant) and isinstance(node.value, (int, float)):
            new = ast.parse(text)
            flipped = False
            for n2 in ast.walk(new):
                if isinstance(n2, ast.Constant) and isinstance(n2.value, (int, float)) \
                        and not isinstance(n2.value, bool):
                    n2.value = n2.value + 1
                    flipped = True
                    break
            return ast.unparse(new) if flipped else None
    return None


def _mutate_stub_body(text: str, tree: ast.Module):
    new = ast.parse(text)
    for n2 in ast.walk(new):
        if isinstance(n2, ast.FunctionDef):
            n2.body = [ast.Return(value=ast.Constant(value=None))]
            return ast.unparse(new)
    return None


def mutation_test(task) -> MutationReport:
    """Plant known-corrupt mutants of `task`'s gold and report the fraction the oracle flags as
    corruption. A gold that fails its own tests would make this meaningless, so mutants are only
    counted when the gold itself passes (a precondition the caller/test asserts)."""
    mutants = _plant_mutants(task)
    caught, escaped = 0, []
    for label, files in mutants:
        v = evaluate_corruption(task, files, merged_clean=True)
        if v.corrupt:
            caught += 1
        else:
            escaped.append(f"{label} (stage={v.stage})")
    n = len(mutants)
    return MutationReport(n_mutants=n, n_caught=caught,
                          catch_rate=(caught / n if n else 0.0), escaped=escaped)

"""U10 — the schedule-independence harness (plan 2026-07-31-001, R14).

The CONVERGENCE metric: run a task's concurrent edits under K different agent orderings and hash
the committed artifact each time. % byte-identical is the schedule-independence of that commit
policy. This is EICO's H2 claim (commit is independent of the schedule/interleaving) made
measurable — and, crucially, a REGRESSION GUARD for U1's canonical order (memory
`planner-order-sensitivity-latent-bug`): a commit that is order-independent only because of a
canonical tie-break will silently become order-SENSITIVE if that canonicalization regresses, and
this harness catches the drop below 1.0.

The harness is policy-agnostic: it takes a `commit_fn(task, order) -> {path: text}` and measures.
It is exercised against the U9 arms (CRDT converges → 1.0; MTPO on a contended tier → < 1.0) and
against EICO's own streaming Coordinator (`eico_commit`), so the metric is grounded in the real
commit path, not only the baselines.

Hashes are taken in PROJECTION space (`render(project(text))`) so pure formatting (blank lines,
annotations the projection doesn't model) never masquerades as a schedule difference — only a
genuine difference in committed structure counts.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from itertools import permutations

from eico.projection.python import project, render
from eico.streaming import Coordinator
from kernel.lift.lift import lift_file


@dataclass
class ScheduleIndependence:
    n_orders: int
    n_distinct: int
    fraction_identical: bool          # True iff every order committed the same artifact
    modal_hash: str
    hashes: dict = field(default_factory=dict)   # order (tuple) -> artifact hash
    schedule_independent: bool = False


def _agents_of(task) -> list:
    seen: list = []
    for edits in getattr(task, "coupling_probe", {}).values():
        for e in edits:
            if e.agent not in seen:
                seen.append(e.agent)
    return seen


def _artifact_hash(files: dict) -> str:
    payload = "\n".join(f"{p}\n{render(project(t))}" for p, t in sorted(files.items()))
    return hashlib.sha256(payload.encode()).hexdigest()[:16]


def _orders(task, k: int = None) -> list:
    agents = _agents_of(task)
    perms = list(permutations(agents))
    if k is not None:
        perms = perms[:k]
    return [list(p) for p in perms] or [[]]


def measure_schedule_independence(task, commit_fn, *, k: int = None) -> ScheduleIndependence:
    """Run `commit_fn(task, order)` under each agent ordering (all permutations, or the first `k`)
    and report whether every order committed the byte-identical (projection-normalized) artifact."""
    hashes = {}
    for order in _orders(task, k):
        files = commit_fn(task, order)
        hashes[tuple(order)] = _artifact_hash(files)
    distinct = set(hashes.values())
    modal = max(distinct, key=lambda h: sum(1 for v in hashes.values() if v == h)) if distinct else ""
    return ScheduleIndependence(
        n_orders=len(hashes), n_distinct=len(distinct),
        fraction_identical=(len(distinct) <= 1), modal_hash=modal, hashes=hashes,
        schedule_independent=(len(distinct) <= 1))


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# EICO's own commit path — the streaming Coordinator
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def _order_edits(edits, order):
    names = order if order else [e.agent for e in edits]
    return sorted(edits, key=lambda e: (names.index(e.agent) if e.agent in names else len(names),
                                        e.agent))


def eico_commit(task, order=None) -> dict:
    """Drive EICO's streaming Coordinator over each file's concurrent drafts in the given agent
    order and render the committed artifact. This is the real EICO commit path H2 concerns: a
    commuting task must converge to one artifact regardless of order; a non-commuting task
    converges only via the invariant-confluence gate + canonical resolution (U1)."""
    files = {}
    for path, edits in getattr(task, "coupling_probe", {}).items():
        base = task.files.get(path, "")
        base_art = project(base)
        ordered = _order_edits(edits, order)
        lifts = {e.agent: lift_file(base, e.after, agent=e.agent) for e in ordered}
        coord = Coordinator(base_art, agent_bounds=None, agents={e.agent for e in ordered})
        for e in ordered:
            for eff in lifts[e.agent].eico_effects():
                coord.on_effect(eff)
        for e in ordered:
            coord.on_agent_done(e.agent)
        coord.quiesce()
        files[path] = render(coord.cur)
    return files

def eico_commit_detail(task, order=None) -> tuple[dict, int]:
    """Drive EICO's REAL commit path — the full `Proxy` (sessions, `write_file` admission, `done`,
    quiescence) — over each file's concurrent drafts in the given agent order, exactly as
    `kernel.harness.footprints._drive` does. Returns `(committed_files, held_total)`.

    This is the faithful path H2 concerns, and it is materially different from driving the raw
    `Coordinator`: on a contended cell the Proxy HOLDS the losing edit (surfaces the conflict as a
    Verdict) rather than silently last-writer-overwriting it. So on T2/T3 `held_total > 0` and the
    rendered artifact is the SAFELY-ADMITTED subset with the contested edit withheld — not a silent
    corruption. A caller feeding this to the oracle passes `merged_clean = (held_total == 0)`, so a
    held (surfaced) conflict is never counted as silent corruption."""
    files, held_total = {}, 0
    for path, edits in getattr(task, "coupling_probe", {}).items():
        base = task.files.get(path, "")
        proxy = Proxy()
        proxy.register_file(path, base)
        ordered = _order_edits(edits, order)
        for e in ordered:
            proxy.start_session(e.agent)
            proxy.read_file(e.agent, path)
        for e in ordered:                      # both submit before either is done: the eventual
            proxy.write_file(e.agent, path, e.after)   # resolution lands in the log
        for e in ordered:
            proxy.done(e.agent)
        proxy.quiesce_all()
        coord = proxy.workspace.coordinator(path)
        held_total += len(coord.ctrl.log.held)
        files[path] = proxy.workspace.render(path)
    return files, held_total


def eico_commit(task, order=None) -> dict:
    """The committed artifact from EICO's real Proxy path (drops the held count; see
    `eico_commit_detail`). Schedule-independence is measured over this render."""
    files, _held = eico_commit_detail(task, order)
    return files
